summary.title: HoneNode — STRIDE threat model (AgileCTI)
summary.description: Threat model developed by AgileCTI (fictitious CTI provider). Subject of test: HoneNode, developed by SharpNode SP. Methodology: STRIDE, OWASP Threat Dragon. Scope: the HoneNode management plane (app + honed broker), the tenant isolation model, the edge/WAF chain and the four demo services (static blog, shop database, media vault, git forge).

diagrams.title: HoneNode — platform overview (STRIDE)
diagrams.description: Trust boundaries and STRIDE threats for the HoneNode management plane and tenant isolation model.

threats.title: Anonymous internet traffic reaches tenant sites
threats.description: Any internet client can reach tenant vhosts through the edge; the edge must not confuse tenants.
threats.mitigation: Caddy routes by validated hostname; the app validates tenant/service/hostname ownership before rendering a vhost.

threats.title: Credential stuffing against the shared login panel
threats.description: Tenants and the operator share one login panel; account numbers are bearer identifiers.
threats.mitigation: 12-digit Luhn account numbers, argon2id, per-account and global rate limits, fail2ban, KDF cost for unknown accounts.

threats.title: Operator dashboard exposed to the internet
threats.description: The operator console grants tenant, plan and quota administration.
threats.mitigation: Loopback-only listener, SSH tunnel, documented exposure model; never an unprotected public listener.

threats.title: Tenant hostname takeover or vhost misrouting
threats.description: A tenant could claim another tenant's hostname or receive traffic for a vhost it does not own.
threats.mitigation: Validate tenant/service/hostname ownership in the app before rendering vhosts; per-host TLS; no wildcard sharing.

threats.title: Edge connection flood
threats.description: Public 80/443 is the only public HTTP surface and can be saturated.
threats.mitigation: WAF rate limiting, fail2ban, connection limits; edge logs feed per-vhost bandwidth accounting.

threats.title: CRS bypass via encoding or parser mismatch
threats.description: A crafted request may evade ModSecurity rules while the upstream app still parses it.
threats.mitigation: Pinned image, DetectionOnly → tune → On rollout, ZAP regression, rule updates.

threats.title: Request bodies or tokens captured in audit logs
threats.description: ModSecurity audit logs can contain credentials if bodies are logged.
threats.mitigation: Audit parts exclude request bodies on auth paths; redaction before shipping.

threats.title: Session cookie theft via XSS
threats.description: A stolen session cookie impersonates the tenant or operator.
threats.mitigation: HttpOnly, SameSite, Secure cookies; strict CSP without inline; no third-party origins.

threats.title: CSRF on state-changing routes
threats.description: A cross-site form could provision, delete or redeem on behalf of a logged-in user.
threats.mitigation: Per-session CSRF token on every state-changing form; SameSite cookies.

threats.title: App compromise escalates to host authority
threats.description: The app renders tenant input and runs next to the host agent.
threats.mitigation: Unprivileged app, no Podman socket, no shell, no tenant sockets; only typed broker calls over a Unix socket.

threats.title: Secrets rendered by inspection or console views
threats.description: Inspection endpoints could return environment values or password hashes.
threats.mitigation: Keys-only projections, hostile-answer validation, no DB console; secret values never stored in app SQL.

threats.title: First-run operator credentials exposed in logs
threats.description: Generated operator credentials are printed once to the journal and written to a bootstrap file.
threats.mitigation: Mode-0600 bootstrap file, single WARN line, save-and-delete instruction, restricted journal access.

threats.title: Missing audit for denied actions
threats.description: A denied login, key redemption or provisioning attempt could leave no trace.
threats.mitigation: Audit events for login, signup, keys, provisioning and lifecycle, including denials.

threats.title: Rogue local process connects to the broker socket
threats.description: Any local process that can open the socket could request host actions.
threats.mitigation: Socket 0660 root:platform group, peer-UID audit, typed operations, root-owned policy.

threats.title: Command or unit injection through free-form arguments
threats.description: The broker writes Quadlet units and runs systemctl as root.
threats.mitigation: Typed arguments only, names derived from tenant IDs, allowlist regexes, no interpolation into Exec=/Volume=/Environment=.

threats.title: Operator policy swapped by a non-root process
threats.description: The policy is the authorization source for plans and limits.
threats.mitigation: Root-owned policy, O_NOFOLLOW, per-call load and validation, 64 KiB cap.

threats.title: Reservation exhaustion via repeated provisioning
threats.description: A tenant could consume host CPU/memory reservations with repeated requests.
threats.mitigation: Reservations and tombstones, host CPU budget, per-tenant caps, jobs and audit trail.

threats.title: Registry file modified by a tenant
threats.description: The registry holds accounts, sessions, plans and audit.
threats.mitigation: 0600 app-user-owned file, no network surface, parameterized SQL, WAL single-writer.

threats.title: Backups contain password hashes and audit PII
threats.description: Offline backups replicate credentials and personal data.
threats.mitigation: VACUUM INTO plus encrypted off-host storage when configured; retention policy.

threats.title: Secret environment files readable by the tenant
threats.description: Database and Forgejo secrets live in root-owned env files.
threats.mitigation: Root-owned 0600 files, broker-only writes, keys-only inspection in the panel.

threats.title: Container escape to the host
threats.description: A kernel or runtime escape would break the per-tenant UID boundary.
threats.mitigation: Rootless Podman, no privileges, no host mounts, SELinux on the target, seccomp defaults, patched kernel.

threats.title: Cross-tenant data or network access
threats.description: Tenants share one host and one loopback.
threats.mitigation: One UID and netns per tenant, internal networks, no loopback mapping, no shared volumes.

threats.title: Noisy neighbour saturates the host
threats.description: One tenant workload could starve the others.
threats.mitigation: cgroup v2 MemoryHigh/Max, CPUWeight/Quota, TasksMax, PidsLimit; PSI telemetry phase 2.

threats.title: Tenant workload reaches host loopback, registry or WAF
threats.description: Loopback-published services and the broker socket must stay unreachable from containers.
threats.mitigation: pasta --no-map-gw, internal network without default route, host firewall.

threats.title: Volume data survives deletion longer than policy
threats.description: Deleting a service does not erase its volume data.
threats.mitigation: Documented retention and purge procedure; operator-mediated erasure.

threats.title: Unsigned or unpinned images pulled at start
threats.description: Tenant workloads pull images at activation time.
threats.mitigation: Registry allowlist, pinned digests, Trivy/SBOM, signed registry (proposed).

threats.title: Image name confusion or typosquatting
threats.description: A lookalike image could be approved by mistake.
threats.mitigation: Fully qualified references validated against the root catalog; allowed registries only.

threats.title: SIEM credentials or logs leak to tenants
threats.description: Approved logs include account identifiers and source IPs.
threats.mitigation: Read-only role, root-only HEC token, no browser access, TLS, retention configured.

threats.title: Untrusted CTI data reaches the hosting plane
threats.description: MISP ingests untrusted third-party data.
threats.mitigation: Isolated network, gated activation, loopback UI, no shared network with panel, registry or tenants.

threats.title: Forged actor metadata in broker requests
threats.description: The app asserts the actor; the broker must not trust it blindly.
threats.mitigation: Peer-UID audit, typed operations, policy revalidation per call; asserted actor is logged, not authoritative.

data.name: Writes units and secrets as root

threats.title: Registry egress used for data exfiltration
threats.description: Host egress exists for image pulls; a compromised workload could try to reuse it.
threats.mitigation: Egress only at pull time to allowlisted registries; tenant workloads have no egress; firewall allowlist.

diagrams.title: Tenant service plane — four demo services (STRIDE)
diagrams.description: Per-tenant isolation, loopback publication and the four demo services: blog, shop database, media vault and git forge.

threats.title: Per-tenant bandwidth exhaustion
threats.description: Tenant traffic crosses the edge; one tenant can saturate the link.
threats.mitigation: Edge/WAF rate limiting; per-vhost accounting from Caddy access logs.

threats.title: Tenant content defacement
threats.description: The blog content is writable by the tenant.
threats.mitigation: Content owned by the tenant; no host mounts; backups and audit.

threats.title: Database brute force on loopback
threats.description: The database is published on 127.0.0.1:15521.
threats.mitigation: scram-sha-256, loopback-only publication, operator-mediated console, fail2ban.

threats.title: Database credentials exposed
threats.description: The broker generates the database password.
threats.mitigation: Root-owned 0600 env file, never stored in app SQL, jobs or audit.

threats.title: File-manager settings relabeled by the tenant
threats.description: The settings file is root-owned; the tenant's Podman cannot relabel it.
threats.mitigation: Broker labels the file for containers; mount is read-only without :Z.

threats.title: Media vault exposed without MIME inspection or quota
threats.description: Uploaded media is served without MIME inspection; disk quota is not applied.
threats.mitigation: Operator decision required; MIME inspection and quota are not integrated.

threats.title: First-run install page takeover
threats.description: Forgejo serves an install page until the admin account exists.
threats.mitigation: Complete the admin account immediately after activation; loopback-only until then.

threats.title: Git SSH brute force on the public port
threats.description: The git SSH port (22091) is a public exception.
threats.mitigation: Key-only authentication, dedicated port, fail2ban, allowlist.

threats.title: Volume data readable across services of the same tenant
threats.description: All services of one tenant share the tenant UID.
threats.mitigation: Same-tenant trust domain is documented; per-service UID separation is future work.

threats.title: Secret values rendered in the panel
threats.description: Inspection could expose environment values.
threats.mitigation: Keys-only inspection, redaction, root-only files.

threats.title: Operator tunnel compromise
threats.description: The operator reaches the database through a loopback tunnel.
threats.mitigation: SSH keys only, loopback binding, audit of operator actions.
